title: ipomoea triloba f. lacunosa
intro: Ipomoea triloba f. lacunosa, commonly known as "Blue Starvine", is a type of flowering vine native to tropical Asia. It is a plant that is valued for its potential health benefits, including being used to treat fever, rheumatism, and other inflammatory conditions due to its anti-inflammatory and antipyretic properties. The therapeutic actions of Blue Starvine are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include alkaloids, flavonoids, and glycosides, such as calystegine and ipomeanol, that exhibit analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities. Additionally, studies have shown that the plant's extracts may also have antimicrobial and antiviral properties, making it a promising candidate for further research in the development of new medicines.
